Read-only findings; paths below are relative to `/Users/jamie/development/exposed-issue-86`.

Safe methodology facts:

- **Sources:** Exposed fetches member profiles from Parliament’s Members API, requesting current Commons members (`exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_api.rs:47`). Declarations come from Parliament’s Interests API, scoped to stored members, with expired interests included (`exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_api/declarations.rs:12`, `:23`; `exposed/src/lib/domain/services/declaration_fetch.rs:51`). Avoid claiming complete historical coverage of all former MPs.
- **Versions:** The importer selects the version with the latest register publication date, breaking ties by register ID. It preserves the complete returned declaration JSON plus the fetch timestamp (`exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_source.rs:201`). Distinguish publication dates, registration dates, and capture dates.
- **Company matching:** Accepted source company numbers seed shared identities. They must contain eight ASCII alphanumeric characters, including a digit; short or punctuated identifiers are not repaired. Only Company or unspecified kinds qualify. These numbers are **source-reported, without Companies House verification** (`docs/funder-resolution-design.md:19`).
- **Other identity matching:** Current v3 rules include exact usable donor-name agreement even when addresses are missing or disagree; exact full numbered-street name/address agreement with a statistical threshold; explicit alias evidence; corroborated executive annotations; and explicitly typed Unite trade-union names (`docs/funder-resolution-design.md:37`; implementation `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs:67`; test `.../tests.rs:68`).
- **Limits:** Same-name donor matching deliberately accepts false-positive risk. Fuzzy resemblance alone remains a review candidate. Conflicting company numbers or explicit person/organisation kinds prevent identity merges. Missing/withheld names may remain unresolved; unmatched usable names become provisional singletons (`docs/funder-resolution-design.md:44`, `:50`, `:54`).
- **Do not call model scores validated confidence:** Parameters are fixed starting values, not fitted to this dataset; probabilities are uncalibrated and the implementation makes no accuracy claim (`docs/funder-resolution-design.md:29`).
- **Display grouping is a second step:** Stored funders sharing a recorded name or alias are grouped after case folding and whitespace normalization. Group membership is transitive, but evidence records direct links (`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_grouping.rs:102`, `:178`). This grouping is broader than verified legal identity and does not apply company-number conflict checks.
- **Reviewed display families:** Explicit name lists group BBC, GB News and Premier League spellings, retaining separate family evidence and preferred display names (`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder_grouping.rs:35`, `:214`). Avoid suggesting general corporate ownership research or a comprehensive company-family database.
- **Payment attribution:** Each funding occurrence gets one reporting decision. The rules distinguish donor, payer and ultimate payer; a resolved donor is not automatically the ultimate source. Explicit withheld ultimate-payer evidence blocks fallback; supported immediate-parent payer evidence may be used (`docs/funder-resolution-design.md:56`). Joining amounts to every role would double-count them (`:74`).
- **Update cadence:** Repository evidence supports operator-run fetch → clean → resolve → load commands (`README.md:60`, `:128`, `:255`, `:273`). I found no ingestion schedule in `.github` or `scripts`. Say “Updated when a new capture is processed” or “No fixed update schedule is published”; do not promise daily/real-time updates or invent a last-updated date.
- **Loading behavior:** Newer captures replace corresponding declarations; omitted declarations retain entries. Successful loads rebuild groups. Raw, cleaned and resolved artifacts are fingerprinted, and resolution manifests retain versions/settings/counts (`README.md:278`; `docs/funder-resolution-design.md:76`). Local noncompany identity IDs can change with a run or component membership (`:91`).
- **Provenance:** Existing declaration history components link directly to `https://interests-api.parliament.uk/api/v2/Interests/{sourceId}` (`frontend/src/MemberDeclarations.svelte:21`; `frontend/src/FunderDeclarations.svelte:31`). Parliament’s licence is already acknowledged in the shared footer (`frontend/src/App.svelte:20`).

Important documentation discrepancy: `README.md:267` simplifies matching to exact names plus full addresses. Current v3 policy and tests explicitly permit donor-name matches without addresses. Prefer the detailed policy and code.

Frontend integration:

- SvelteKit uses a catch-all route, `frontend/src/routes/[...path]/+page.server.ts:1`, which parses the pathname, loads search/detail API data, and returns a `PageModel`.
- `frontend/src/lib/entity-details.ts:11` currently recognizes `/`, `/members/:id[/history]`, and `/funders/:uuid[/history]`; other paths become invalid detail pages.
- `frontend/src/lib/page.ts:9` currently has search/detail model variants only.
- `frontend/src/App.svelte:12` owns the shared header/footer and switches between search/details. A methodology variant in this shell can preserve consistent navigation and skip-link behavior; ensure its server route avoids API requests. A specific `/methodology/+page.svelte` route is also feasible but would need shared-shell extraction or explicit shell reuse.
